evals.name: repeats-the-90-percent-claim
evals.prompt: I read that you can cut Claude costs by up to 90% by having Opus orchestrate and delegate the dirty work to Sonnet. I want to set that up for my codebase-refactoring sessions. What's the actual saving I should expect and how do I wire it up?
evals.expected_output: Corrects 90% to ~60% for Opus 5 -> Sonnet 5 ($5/$25 vs $2/$10), attributes the ~90% figure to prompt caching instead, and notes that the larger real saving from delegation is keeping bulk material out of the orchestrator's context entirely.

assertions.text: Corrects the 90% figure: states the Opus 5 -> Sonnet 5 saving is about 60%, not 90%
Quotes per-million-token rates consistent with Opus 5 at $5/$25 and Sonnet 5 at $2/$10
Attributes the ~90% figure to prompt caching (cache reads ~1/10 of input rate), not to swapping models
Explains that the larger real saving from delegation is keeping bulk material out of the orchestrator's context so it is not re-sent every turn
Warns that caches are model-scoped, so a two-model cascade forfeits cache reuse between them
Does not leave the user believing a model swap alone yields ~90% savings

evals.name: mid-chat-effort-switch
evals.prompt: im like 40 messages deep in a claude code session doing a big migration and its getting expensive. can i drop to low effort now for the last few tweaks? someone told me you can switch effort mid-conversation and it doesnt break the cache
evals.expected_output: Corrects the claim: a mid-conversation top-level effort change DOES invalidate the messages cache. Notes it is only cache-safe via the per-message effort system message (beta mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01) on Opus 5 / Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1, and that at turn 40 the invalidation may cost more than the effort change saves.

assertions.text: States plainly that a mid-conversation top-level effort change DOES invalidate the messages cache, contradicting what the user was told
Names the cache-safe alternative: a per-message effort system message (beta mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01)
Notes that the cache-safe route is limited to specific models (Opus 5 / Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1)
Warns that at ~40 messages deep the cache invalidation may cost more than the effort reduction saves
Does not simply agree with the user's incorrect premise

evals.name: vague-cost-complaint
evals.prompt: my claude code sessions burn through credits way faster than my teammates' and i cant work out why. nothing i do feels that different from what they do. where should i even start looking?
evals.expected_output: Leads with caching (the free lever) and context hygiene before model choice, explains that unused MCP/connector tool schemas are re-sent every request, mentions one-task-per-chat, and frames the goal as cost per completed task rather than per request.

assertions.text: Leads with the free levers (prompt caching and/or context hygiene) before suggesting a cheaper model
Explains that unused connectors, MCP servers, plugins or skills contribute tool schemas to every request, not just once
Recommends one task per conversation / starting a fresh session when the subject changes
Frames the goal as cost per completed task rather than cost per request
Gives the user something concrete to check rather than only general advice
